newsitem.title: FRANCE: UAP to sell up to 30 pct of Scor.
newsitem.headline: UAP to sell up to 30 pct of Scor.

text.p: French insurer UAP said on Monday in a statement that it would sell up to 30 percent of its shares in reinsurer Scor via a placement in the United States and elsewhere in the world during the next few weeks.
UAP said it was timing the sale to coincide with Scor's plans to debut on Wall Street, which Scor said in a separate statement would occur in mid-October.

UAP said some seven million shares representing 26 percent of Scor's capital would be put up for sale. The banks in charge of the placement operation would be given a "greenshoe" option for a 1.05 further shares representing an additional four percent of Scor's capital to meet excess demand.
UAP said that it planned to remain a "significant shareholder in Scor."
Union des Assurances de Paris (UAP) had announced earlier this year that it was considering reducing its 40.9 percent stake in the leading French reinsurer.
UAP said the sale would complete the debt reduction programme it launched last spring.
Scor said it was on the point of filing a preliminary prospectus with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission paving the way for its listing.
Scor said Goldman Sachs International and JP Morgan Securities Ltd would be in charge of the operation.
A UAP official said on Monday that the sale of its Scor shares would allow the company to achieve its goal of reducing its 12 billion franc debt by half by the end of 1996.

He said UAP had already reduced its debt by four billion francs through the listing of its Sun Life and Provincial Holding unit in London and that the sale of German insurance operations had raised a further 500 million francs. UAP also recently sold some operations in Chile.
